title: Old, stopped: quadratic reciprocity, qr-1 carried on to 600 rounds. Not fair: shared and OSO turns cost twice as much; replaced by the current run (Nov 26)
question: With the full money ($8 a run) instead of the 100 rounds that stopped qr-1 at about $1.10, does any way of organizing four labs get through the hard middle of quadratic reciprocity (Wilson's theorem, Euler's criterion, Gauss's lemma), and does OSO pull ahead of working alone and of sharing there? One run each: a first look. [A]
answer: Not a fair comparison: stopped early. Shared and OSO labs read the whole library every turn and paid about twice as much a turn as traditional labs, so at the same money traditional got about twice the turns. With that handicap, by $6.80 a run working alone reached 96 hidden steps of 206, the shared library 81, OSO 78; all stopped at level 10 of 17. Traditional's labs repeated each other: 72 of its 96 steps were reached by two or more labs. Unique lemmas: 1,251, 833, 879. Replaced by qr-2, where every setup sees the same 60 lemmas and searches the rest. One run each.

targets.text: Quadratic reciprocity, from scratch: for two different odd primes p and q, q is a square remainder mod p exactly when p is one mod q, unless both p and q leave remainder 3 when divided by 4; then exactly one of them is.
targets.statement: : ∀ p q : N, Prime p → Prime q → p ≠ q → two < p → two < q → ((IsSq p q ↔ IsSq q p) ↔ (ModEq (two * two) p 1 ∨ ModEq (two * two) q 1))

areas: Numbers from scratch (deep set): addition, multiplication, order, divisibility, primes, binomial coefficients and congruences, built from zero and successor.
Quadratic reciprocity (QR set): remainders, products over a range, counting, and squares mod a prime, on the same numbers built from zero and successor.
